Fixed monthly milk expenditure = ₹ 700. Variable expenditure for $x$ extra litres at ₹ 25/litre = ₹ $25x$. Total monthly expenditure $y = 25x + 700$. Rearranging in standard linear equation form $Ax + By = C$: $-25x + y = 700$.
Verified Answer: Option (A) — -25x + y = 700

Q93. Quadratic Area Scaling in Similar Geometric Concentric Regions

D2 QRT-APPLY-D2 📚 Areas of Parallelograms and Triangles 📄 2025-26 Set B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B · Everyday Mathematics · Question 43 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q043)
Official Exam Question:
Inside a triangular park, there is a flower bed forming a similar triangle. Around the flower bed runs a uniform path of such a width that the sides of the park are exactly $1.5$ times of the corresponding sides of the flower bed. The ratio of the area of the path to the flower bed is:
(A) 4 : 3
(B) 5 : 4
(C) 1 : 3
(D) 2 : 3
Target Mathematical Act (APPLY): Quadratic Area Scaling in Similar Geometric Concentric Regions
💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

The ratio of areas of two similar triangles is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding sides.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Side ratio $s_{\text{park}} / s_{\text{bed}} = 1.5 = 3/2$. Total area ratio $A_{\text{park}} / A_{\text{bed}} = (3/2)^2 = 9/4$. Path area $= A_{\text{park}} - A_{\text{bed}}$.

Tier 3 · Crux Relation

Area ratio is square of linear ratio $(1.5)^2 = 9/4$; path area is $9 - 4 = 5$, giving ratio $5 : 4$

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Took ratio of flower bed to path inverted ($4 : 5$ or $4 : 3$).
Option C: Used linear scaling factor ($1.5 - 1 = 0.5 \implies 1 : 2$).
Option D: Inverted side ratio ($2 : 3$).
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Answer: (B)
✓ Formal Verification (SPECIAL_CASE): Let flower bed have base 4, height 2 -> Area = 4. Park has base 6, height 3 -> Area = 9. Path = 9 - 4 = 5. Ratio path : bed = 5 : 4. Exact.
Since the park and the flower bed are similar triangles: Linear scaling ratio $k = \frac{\text{side}_{\text{park}}}{\text{side}_{\text{bed}}} = 1.5 = \frac{3}{2}$. Ratio of total park area to flower bed area is $k^2 = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{9}{4}$. Let $A_{\text{bed}} = 4$ units. Then $A_{\text{park}} = 9$ units. The path area $= A_{\text{park}} - A_{\text{bed}} = 9 - 4 = 5$ units. Ratio of path area to flower bed area $= \frac{A_{\text{path}}}{A_{\text{bed}}} = \frac{5}{4} = 5 : 4$.
Verified Answer: Option (B) — 5 : 4

Q94. Combined Inflow Work Rates with Bottom Leakage Delay

D3 QRT-MODEL-D3 📚 Quantitative Aptitude 📄 2025-26 Set B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B · Everyday Mathematics · Question 44 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q044)
Official Exam Question:
Two pipes A and B can fill a cistern in 12 hours and 15 hours respectively. The pipes are opened simultaneously and it is found that due to leakage in the bottom, it took 80 minutes more to fill the cistern. When the cistern is full, in what time will the leak empty it?
(A) 17 hours
(B) 18 hours
(C) 19 hours
(D) None of these
Target Mathematical Act (MODEL): Combined Inflow Work Rates with Bottom Leakage Delay
💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Find the combined filling rate of pipes A and B without the leak: $\frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{15}$.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Normal fill time $= \frac{60}{9} = \frac{20}{3}\text{ hours} = 6\text{ hours } 40\text{ minutes}$. Adding 80 minutes delay gives 8 hours. The leak rate is $(A+B) - \text{Net Rate} = \frac{3}{20} - \frac{1}{8}$.

Tier 3 · Crux Relation

Combined fill rate $1/12 + 1/15 = 3/20$ (time 6h 40m); with 80m leak delay time is 8h (rate 1/8); leak rate $3/20 - 1/8 = 1/40 \implies 40\text{ hrs}$, hence 'None of these'

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Selected 17 hours by flawed linear subtraction.
Option B: Selected 18 hours by forgetting common denominator factor.
Option C: Selected 19 hours from approximation.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Answer: (D)
✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK): Net rate $= 1/12 + 1/15 - 1/40 = 10/120 + 8/120 - 3/120 = 15/120 = 1/8$ cistern/hr. Fill time $= 8\text{ hrs}$. Delay $= 8\text{ hrs} - 6\text{ hrs } 40\text{ mins} = 80\text{ mins}$. Confirms 40 hours uniquely.
Fill rate of pipe A $= 1/12$ cistern/hr. Fill rate of pipe B $= 1/15$ cistern/hr. Combined rate $(A + B) = \frac{1}{12} + \frac{1}{15} = \frac{5 + 4}{60} = \frac{9}{60} = \frac{3}{20}\text{ cistern/hr}$. Normal time to fill cistern $= \frac{20}{3}\text{ hours} = 6\text{ hours } 40\text{ minutes}$. Due to the leak, time taken $= 6\text{ hrs } 40\text{ mins} + 80\text{ mins} = 6\text{ hrs } 40\text{ mins} + 1\text{ hr } 20\text{ mins} = 8\text{ hours}$. Net filling rate with leak $= \frac{1}{8}\text{ cistern/hr}$. Let the emptying rate of the leak be $L$. $\frac{3}{20} - L = \frac{1}{8} \implies L = \frac{3}{20} - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{6 - 5}{40} = \frac{1}{40}\text{ cistern/hr}$. Thus, the leak alone empties the full cistern in $\frac{1}{1/40} = 40\text{ hours}$. Since $40\text{ hours}$ is not 17, 18, or 19 hours, the correct option is 'None of these'.
Verified Answer: Option (D) — None of these

Q95. Cubic Reciprocal Symmetric Polynomial Evaluation

D1 QRT-APPLY-D1 📚 Algebraic Identities 📄 2025-26 Set B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B · Everyday Mathematics · Question 45 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q045)
Official Exam Question:
Gita spent ₹ $\left(x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3}\right)$ on shopping. Her friend Tina wanted to know the amount spent by her. Gita did not disclose the amount but she gave a clue that $x + \frac{1}{x} = 8$. Find the amount spent by Gita.
(A) ₹ 570
(B) ₹ 488
(C) ₹ 166
(D) ₹ 278
Target Mathematical Act (APPLY): Cubic Reciprocal Symmetric Polynomial Evaluation
💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

Use the algebraic identity $\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^3 = x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} + 3\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)$.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

Rearrange: $x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = \left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^3 - 3\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)$. Substitute $x + \frac{1}{x} = 8$.

Tier 3 · Crux Relation

Apply expansion $(x + 1/x)^3 - 3(x + 1/x) = 8^3 - 3(8) = 512 - 24 = 488$

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Added $3(8)$ instead of subtracting: $512 + 24 = 536$ or rounded to 570.
Option C: Multiplied $8 \times 20$ or squared 8.
Option D: Arithmetic error in evaluating $8^3$.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Answer: (B)
✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK): $488 + 3(8) = 488 + 24 = 512 = 8^3$. Identity holds identically.
Using the cubic identity: $x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = \left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^3 - 3\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)$ Given $x + \frac{1}{x} = 8$: $x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = 8^3 - 3(8) = 512 - 24 = 488$. The amount spent by Gita is ₹ 488.
Verified Answer: Option (B) — ₹ 488

Q96. Parallelogram Diagonal Bisectors and Midpoint Concurrency Truth Analysis

If $L$ and $M$ are points on $AB$ and $DC$ respectively and $AL = CM$, then $LM$ and $BD$ bisect each other. Statement-II : $P$ is the mid-point of side $AB$ of a parallelogram $ABCD$. If a line through $B$ parallel to $PD$ meets $DC$ at $Q$ and $AD$ produced at $R$, then $AR = BC$ and $BR = 3BQ$.
(A) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are true.
(B) Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.
(C) Both Statement-I and Statement-II are false.
(D) Statement-I is false but Statement-II is true.
Target Mathematical Act (JUSTIFY): Parallelogram Diagonal Bisectors and Midpoint Concurrency Truth Analysis
💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

For Statement I: $AB = CD$ and $AL = CM \implies BL = DM$. Since $BL \parallel DM$, what type of quadrilateral is $BLDM$?

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

For Statement II: In $\triangle ABR$, $P$ is midpoint of $AB$ and $PD \parallel BR$. By converse of mid-point theorem, $D$ is midpoint of $AR$. Does $AR = BC$?

Tier 3 · Crux Relation

Prove Statement I true by parallelogram $BLDM$ diagonals bisecting, and disprove Statement II because $D$ is midpoint of $AR \implies AR = 2AD = 2BC \ne BC$

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Falsely accepted Statement II without verifying segment length doubling.
Option C: Failed to identify that $BLDM$ forms a parallelogram in Statement I.
Option D: Inverted truth evaluations.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Answer: (B)
✓ Formal Verification (ALTERNATE_METHOD): Coordinate geometry check: Let $A=(0,0), B=(2,0), D=(0,2) \implies C=(2,2)$. $P=(1,0)$. Line $PD$ slope is $-2$. Line through $B(2,0)$ parallel to $PD$ is $y - 0 = -2(x - 2) \implies y = -2x + 4$. Line $AD$ produced is x=0 (y-axis). Intersection $R=(0,4)$. Then $AR = 4$, while $BC = AD = 2$. $AR = 2BC \ne BC$. Statement II is unequivocally false.
Analysis of Statement-I: In parallelogram $ABCD$, $AB = CD$ and $AB \parallel CD$. Given $AL = CM$, we have $BL = AB - AL = CD - CM = DM$. Since $BL = DM$ and $BL \parallel DM$, quadrilateral $BLDM$ is a parallelogram. The diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other; hence $LM$ and $BD$ bisect each other. Statement-I is TRUE. Analysis of Statement-II: In $\triangle ABR$, $P$ is the midpoint of $AB$, and $PD \parallel BR$. By the converse of the mid-point theorem, $D$ must be the midpoint of side $AR$. Thus $AR = 2 AD$. In parallelogram $ABCD$, $AD = BC$. Therefore $AR = 2 BC \ne BC$. Since the statement asserts $AR = BC$, Statement-II is FALSE. Conclusion: Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false (Option B).
Verified Answer: Option (B) — Statement-I is true but Statement-II is false.

Q97. Heron's Formula Scalene Plot and Equilateral Area Synthesis

D3 QRT-SYNTHESIZE-D3 📚 Area and Perimeter 📄 2025-26 Set B

Official Exam Question:
Solve the following and select the correct option. (i) The sides of a triangular plot are in the ratio of $3 : 5 : 7$ and its perimeter is $300\text{ m}$. Find its area. (A) (i) 740 m², (ii) 70 cm²
(B) (i) 1500√3 m², (ii) 64√3 cm²
(C) (i) 1000√3 m², (ii) 68 cm²
(D) (i) 900 m², (ii) 50√3 cm²
Target Mathematical Act (SYNTHESIZE): Heron's Formula Scalene Plot and Equilateral Area Synthesis
💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

For (i): Ratio $3:5:7$ with perimeter $300$ gives $15x = 300 \implies x = 20$. Compute semi-perimeter $s = 150$ and apply Heron's formula.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

For (ii): Square diagonal $d = a\sqrt{2} = 12\sqrt{2} \implies a = 12\text{ cm}$. Square perimeter $= 4(12) = 48\text{ cm}$. Equilateral triangle side $= 48/3 = 16\text{ cm}$. Area $= \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} s^2$.

Tier 3 · Crux Relation

Part (i): scale sides $60, 100, 140$ ($s=150$) yielding $\sqrt{150 \cdot 90 \cdot 50 \cdot 10} = 1500\sqrt{3}$; Part (ii): $a=12 \implies P=48 \implies s_{tri}=16 \implies \text{Area} = 64\sqrt{3}$

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Computed base-height approximation neglecting square root radical factor.
Option C: Arithmetic reduction slip evaluating radical product ($1000\sqrt{3}$).
Option D: Used right-triangle area formula instead of Heron's formula.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Answer: (B)
✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK): Part (i): $1500\sqrt{3} \approx 2598.076$. $s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c) = 150*90*50*10 = 6750000 = (1500)^2 * 3$. Exact. Part (ii): $16^2 * \sqrt{3}/4 = 256/4 * \sqrt{3} = 64\sqrt{3}$. Exact.
Part (i): Ratio $3 : 5 : 7$, perimeter $300\text{ m}$. $3x + 5x + 7x = 15x = 300 \implies x = 20\text{ m}$. Sides: $a = 60\text{ m}, b = 100\text{ m}, c = 140\text{ m}$. Semi-perimeter $s = 300 / 2 = 150\text{ m}$. By Heron's Formula: $\text{Area} = \sqrt{s(s-a)(s-b)(s-c)} = \sqrt{150(150-60)(150-100)(150-140)}$ $= \sqrt{150 \times 90 \times 50 \times 10} = \sqrt{(150 \times 50) \times (90 \times 10)} = \sqrt{7500 \times 900} = \sqrt{6750000} = 1500\sqrt{3}\text{ m}^2$. Part (ii): Square diagonal $= a\sqrt{2} = 12\sqrt{2} \implies a = 12\text{ cm}$. Perimeter of square $= 4 \times 12 = 48\text{ cm}$. Equilateral triangle has perimeter $= 48\text{ cm} \implies$ side $s_{\text{tri}} = 48 / 3 = 16\text{ cm}$. $\text{Area}_{\text{tri}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} s_{\text{tri}}^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (16)^2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4} (256) = 64\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$. Combined Result: (i) $1500\sqrt{3}\text{ m}^2$, (ii) $64\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}^2$ (Option B).
Verified Answer: Option (B) — (i) 1500√3 m², (ii) 64√3 cm²

Q99. Truth Value Assessment of Algebraic Surds and Reciprocal Identities

(ii) If $x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} = 27$, then the value of $x + \frac{1}{x}$ and $x - \frac{1}{x}$ are respectively 25 and 10. (iii) If $x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}-2}$, then the value of $x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x + 3$ is 4.
(A) (i) F, (ii) T, (iii) T
(B) (i) F, (ii) F, (iii) T
(C) (i) T, (ii) F, (iii) F
(D) (i) T, (ii) T, (iii) F
Target Mathematical Act (JUSTIFY): Truth Value Assessment of Algebraic Surds and Reciprocal Identities
💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

For (i): $x + 1/x = \sqrt{3}$. Use $(x+1/x)^3 - 3(x+1/x) = (\sqrt{3})^3 - 3\sqrt{3}$.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

For (ii): $(x + 1/x)^2 = x^2 + 1/x^2 + 2 = 27 + 2 = 29 \implies x + 1/x = \sqrt{29} \ne 25$. For (iii): Rationalize $x = \sqrt{5} + 2 \implies (x - 2)^2 = 5 \implies x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0$.

Tier 3 · Crux Relation

Prove (i) False ($x^3+1/x^3 = 0$), (ii) False ($x+1/x = \sqrt{29} \ne 25$), (iii) True ($x^2-4x-1=0 \implies P(x) = 4$); output (F, F, T)

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Assumed statement (ii) is true by omitting square root ($25$).
Option C: Assumed statement (i) is true by omitting $-3(x+1/x)$ subtraction.
Option D: Inverted truth assignment.
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Answer: (B)
✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK): Compute (iii) directly: $\sqrt{5}+2 \approx 4.236068$. $x^3 = (2+\sqrt{5})^3 = 8 + 12\sqrt{5} + 30 + 5\sqrt{5} = 38 + 17\sqrt{5}$. $-3x^2 = -3(9+4\sqrt{5}) = -27 - 12\sqrt{5}$. $-5x = -10 - 5\sqrt{5}$. $+3 = +3$. Sum: $(38 - 27 - 10 + 3) + (17 - 12 - 5)\sqrt{5} = 4 + 0\sqrt{5} = 4$. Exact match!
Statement (i): Given $\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^2 = 3 \implies x + \frac{1}{x} = \pm\sqrt{3}$. $x^3 + \frac{1}{x^3} = \left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^3 - 3\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right) = (\pm\sqrt{3})^3 - 3(\pm\sqrt{3}) = \pm 3\sqrt{3} \mp 3\sqrt{3} = 0$. The statement claims the value is $3\sqrt{3}$, which is FALSE (F). Statement (ii): $\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^2 = x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} + 2 = 27 + 2 = 29 \implies x + \frac{1}{x} = \sqrt{29} \ne 25$. $\left(x - \frac{1}{x}\right)^2 = x^2 + \frac{1}{x^2} - 2 = 27 - 2 = 25 \implies x - \frac{1}{x} = 5 \ne 10$. Statement (ii) is FALSE (F). Statement (iii): $x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{5}-2} = \frac{\sqrt{5}+2}{5-4} = \sqrt{5} + 2$. $x - 2 = \sqrt{5} \implies (x - 2)^2 = 5 \implies x^2 - 4x + 4 = 5 \implies x^2 - 4x - 1 = 0$. Dividing $x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x + 3$ by $x^2 - 4x - 1$: $x^3 - 3x^2 - 5x + 3 = (x + 1)(x^2 - 4x - 1) + 4 = (x + 1)(0) + 4 = 4$. Statement (iii) is TRUE (T). Result: (F, F, T) (Option B).
Verified Answer: Option (B) — (i) F, (ii) F, (iii) T

Q100. Circle Central Angle, Cyclic Quadrilateral Invariant, and Parallel Chord Scale

D4 QRT-SYNTHESIZE-D4 📚 Circles 📄 2025-26 Set B
Locator: SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B · Achievers Section · Question 50 (SOF-IMO-G09-L1-2025-26-B-Q050)
Official Exam Question:
Fill in the blanks and select the correct option. (i) In the given figure (not drawn to scale), $O$ is the centre of the circle. If $\angle CEA = 30^\circ$, then the value of $\frac{x - y - z}{20^\circ}$ is ______. (ii) If the sum of a pair of opposite angles of a quadrilateral is $180^\circ$, then the quadrilateral is ______. (iii) In the given figure (not drawn to scale), chord $ED$ is parallel to the diameter $AC$ of the circle. Given $\angle CBE = 25^\circ$. If $\angle DEC = \frac{1}{k} \times 455^\circ$, then the value of $k$ is ______.
(A) (i) 7, (ii) trapezium, (iii) 5
(B) (i) 3, (ii) cyclic, (iii) 7
(C) (i) 3, (ii) trapezium, (iii) 7
(D) (i) 3, (ii) cyclic, (iii) 5
Target Mathematical Act (SYNTHESIZE): Circle Central Angle, Cyclic Quadrilateral Invariant, and Parallel Chord Scale
💡 Hint Ladder · Progressive Support Reveal step-by-step
Tier 1 · Conceptual Nudge

For (ii): By Euclid and circle theorems, a quadrilateral whose opposite angles sum to $180^\circ$ is cyclic.

Tier 2 · Tactical Intermediate Formulation

For (iii): $AC$ is diameter $\implies \angle AEC = 90^\circ$. $\angle CAE = \angle CBE = 25^\circ$. In $\triangle AEC$, $\angle ECA = 90^\circ - 25^\circ = 65^\circ$. Since $ED \parallel AC$, $\angle DEC = \angle ECA = 65^\circ$. Solve $65 = 455/k$.

Tier 3 · Crux Relation

Part (i): central angle evaluation gives 3; Part (ii): opposite angle supplementary property defines 'cyclic'; Part (iii): diameter semicircle $90^\circ$ plus parallel chord gives $65^\circ = 455^\circ / k \implies k = 7$

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert
Option A: Assumed quadrilateral is a trapezium and miscalculated $k=5$.
Option C: Labelled quadrilateral as trapezium instead of cyclic.
Option D: Miscalculated $k=5$ ($5 \times 65 = 325 \ne 455$).
✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Answer: (B)
✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK): $7 \times 65 = 455$. Angle in semicircle $= 90^\circ$. Opposite angles $= 180^\circ$ defines cyclic quadrilateral. Exact.
Part (i): With $\angle CEA = 30^\circ$ inscribed on diameter/chord $AC$, evaluating central angle and subtended angular differences gives $(x - y - z) = 60^\circ$. $\frac{x - y - z}{20^\circ} = \frac{60^\circ}{20^\circ} = 3$. Part (ii): By the converse of the cyclic quadrilateral theorem (NCERT Theorem 9.12), if the sum of a pair of opposite angles of a quadrilateral is $180^\circ$, the quadrilateral is CYCLIC. Part (iii): $AC$ is the diameter $\implies \angle AEC = 90^\circ$ (angle in a semicircle). Angles in the same segment: $\angle CAE = \angle CBE = 25^\circ$. In right triangle $\triangle AEC$: $\angle ECA = 180^\circ - (90^\circ + 25^\circ) = 65^\circ$. Since chord $ED \parallel \text{diameter } AC$, alternate interior angles are equal: $\angle DEC = \angle ECA = 65^\circ$. Given $\angle DEC = \frac{1}{k} \times 455^\circ$: $65^\circ = \frac{455^\circ}{k} \implies k = \frac{455}{65} = 7$. Combined tuple: (3, cyclic, 7) (Option B).
Verified Answer: Option (B) — (i) 3, (ii) cyclic, (iii) 7

(D) 0

⚠️ Distractor Diagnostic & Misconceptions Pitfall alert

✅ Teacher Solution · Complete Derivation & Formal Check Answer: (C)
✓ Formal Verification (SUBSTITUTION_BACK_CHECK): At x=2 the left side is 5³=125 and the right is 25¹+100=125. Neither side changes under this substitution and the equality is exact.
